Atmosphere

Both low and high oxygen can damage animals outside their inherited tolerance. Selection changes descendants; adults do not rewrite their DNA.

Terrain

Water changes traversable habitat. Rugged terrain slows movement; vegetation provides cover and fertility changes food production.

New experiment

Begin with two genetically identical asexual founders. Compare their descendants as mutations and local conditions shape each lineage.

Environment controls act immediately. Restart applies the current atmosphere and terrain to a new population. Brain dimensions require a restart.

Neural inheritance

0 uses foraging, escape, and budding rules. Neural outputs control turning, movement, predatory attacks, and willingness to bud. Mate inputs remain zero in this asexual experiment. Territorial defense uses inherited aggression independently of the neural attack output. Offspring inherit whole network modules from either parent, then mutate.
